target_customer: League of Legends and other competitive gamers (consumers), monetized through content and the companion app
problem: Casual and ranked players want coaching and strategy but pro-level insight is hard to access; the app used computer vision to coach automatically during games.
business_model: Ad and media supported content plus a free desktop coaching app (monetization not detailed in sources)
product_category: Esports media and in-game coaching app

founders.name: Jonathan Lin
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; Forbes 30 Under 30 Media 2019 per a search result summary (not opened).

founders.name: Rick Ling
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; introduced the company on Medium. No background found.

exit.reason: Discord acquired the team; the Blitz app software and brand were then sold to Swift (parent of Team SoloMid) in January 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision reading live League of Legends game state plus data-driven recommendations, built by a small team in 2015.

defensibility.rationale: Dependent on a single game publisher's ecosystem; rivals such as Overwolf-based apps could build similar tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence Riot copied it. Discord acquired the team in November 2018 and Swift acquired the app and brand in January 2019.

market_need_then: Esports audiences were growing and the YC page says the app reached over a million games per week a month into open beta.

branding.community_and_virality: App reached over a million games per week a month after open beta (YC page).

brand_strength.rationale: Brand survived the team sale: Swift bought the software and branding in 2019 and kept the Blitz name, which implies recognized value. No press specifically about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Blitz combined esports media with a computer vision coaching app that reached over a million games per week early in beta. Discord acquired the team in November 2018 and dropped the content side, and Swift bought the app software and brand in January 2019. Terms and funding were not found, so whether it was a strong exit or a team purchase is unclear.
